feedback.problem: What is the remainder when  $27{x}^{3}+8$ is divided by $9{x}^{2}-6x+4?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{2}$ and $x$ terms. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing terms with zero coefficients, as follows:

$$
27{x}^{3}+8=27{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+0x+8
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,3x+2 \\  & 9{x}^{2}-6x+4\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,27{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+0x+8\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{27{x}^{3}-18{x}^{2}+12x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,18{x}^{2}-12x+8 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{18{x}^{2}-12x+8}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

- the quotient is $3x+2,$ and

- the remainder is $0.$
